questions.solution: The Ramon Magsaysay Award is often referred to as the "Nobel Prize of Asia." It was established in 1957 to commemorate the former Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay and is awarded annually to individuals or organizations in Asia who demonstrate selfless service and transformative influence.

The Bharat Ratna was first awarded in 1954. The first recipients were C. Rajagopalachari, Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, and C.V. Raman. It is the highest civilian award of the Republic of India, given for exceptional service towards the advancement of art, literature, science, and public service.

The Pulitzer Prize is given for excellence in newspaper journalism, literary achievements, and musical composition. It was established in 1917 by provisions in the will of Joseph Pulitzer, and is administered by Columbia University. It is one of the most prestigious awards in the field of literature and journalism.

questions.question: The Nobel Prize was established by: नोबेल पुरस्कार की स्थापना किसने की थी:
questions.solution: The Nobel Prize was established by Alfred Nobel, a Swedish chemist, engineer, and industrialist. Alfred Nobel signed his last will and testament on November 27, 1895, giving the largest share of his fortune to establish the Nobel Prizes. The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901.

The Fields Medal is awarded for outstanding contributions to mathematics. It is often viewed as the highest honor a mathematician can receive, and is sometimes described as the "Nobel Prize of Mathematics." It is awarded every four years at the International Congress of Mathematicians to mathematicians under 40 years of age.

The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is given for outstanding contribution to Indian cinema. It is India's highest award in the field of cinema and is presented annually by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. The award was instituted in 1969 in honor of Dadasaheb Phalke, who is regarded as the father of Indian cinema.

The Arjuna Award is given for excellence in sports. It is presented by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, to recognize outstanding achievement in sports. The award was instituted in 1961 and carries a cash prize, a bronze statue of Arjuna, and a scroll.

The Academy Awards are presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. The Academy Awards, popularly known as the Oscars, are awards for artistic and technical merit in the film industry. They are regarded as the most prestigious awards in the entertainment industry and are given annually.

The Jnanpith Award is given for outstanding contribution to Indian literature. It is one of the most prestigious literary awards in India and is presented annually by the Bharatiya Jnanpith to an author for their "outstanding contribution towards literature." The award was instituted in 1961.

Mathematics is not a category for the Nobel Prize. The Nobel Prize is awarded in six categories: Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economic Sciences (officially called the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, added in 1968).

The Man Booker Prize is awarded for the best novel written in English and published in the UK or Ireland. It was established in 1969 and is one of the most prestigious literary prizes in the English-speaking world. The prize aims to promote the finest in fiction by rewarding the best novel of the year.

The Kalinga Prize is awarded by UNESCO for the popularization of science. The Kalinga Prize is an international award given by UNESCO for exceptional skill in presenting scientific ideas to the general public. It was established in 1951 following a donation from Biju Patnaik, the former Chief Minister of Odisha, India.

The Padma Vibhushan is the second highest civilian award in India. The Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian award of the Republic of India, after the Bharat Ratna. It is awarded for "exceptional and distinguished service" in various fields including art, literature, sports, medicine, social work, and public affairs.

The Abel Prize is awarded for outstanding contributions to mathematics. The Abel Prize is awarded annually by the King of Norway to one or more outstanding mathematicians. It is named after Norwegian mathematician Niels Henrik Abel and was established in 2001, with the first award given in 2003.

The Emmy Awards are given for excellence in television in the United States. The Emmy Awards recognize excellence in various aspects of television and emerging media, including acting, writing, and directing. Different categories of Emmy Awards are presented throughout the year, recognizing achievements in daytime, prime time, sports, and news programming.

questions.solution:
Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize - Science and Technology

The Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology is a prestigious science award in India. It was established in 1958 in honor of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar, the founder director of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR). The prize is awarded annually for outstanding contributions to science and technology. It is given in seven different categories: Biological Sciences, Chemical Sciences, Earth, Atmosphere, Ocean and Planetary Sciences, Engineering Sciences, Mathematical Sciences, Medical Sciences, and Physical Sciences. Recipients must be Indian citizens and under 45 years of age.

Pulitzer Prize - Journalism

The Pulitzer Prize is one of the most prestigious awards in journalism, literature, and musical composition in the United States. It was established in 1917 by provisions in the will of Joseph Pulitzer, a Hungarian-American journalist and newspaper publisher. The prizes are administered by Columbia University in New York City. The Pulitzer Prize for journalism is awarded in various categories, including investigative reporting, explanatory reporting, breaking news, and feature writing. The prize aims to recognize excellence in journalism and encourage high standards in the profession.

Pritzker Prize - Architecture

Pritzker Architecture Prize is often referred to as the "Nobel Prize of Architecture." It was established in 1979 by the Pritzker family through their Hyatt Foundation. The prize is awarded annually to a living architect whose built work demonstrates a combination of talent, vision, and commitment. It includes a $100,000 grant and a bronze medallion. The prize is intended to honor a living architect whose work has produced consistent and significant contributions to humanity and the built environment through the art of architecture.

Grammy Awards - Music

The Grammy Awards are presented by the Recording Academy to recognize achievements in the music industry. They were first presented in 1959 and are considered one of the four major annual American entertainment awards, along with the Academy Awards, Emmy Awards, and Tony Awards. The Grammy Awards cover a wide range of music genres and categories, including Record of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year, and Best New Artist. The trophy depicts a gilded gramophone. The awards ceremony is known for its performances by prominent artists and has become a platform for social and political statements.

The Right Livelihood Award is given for practical solutions to global problems. Established in 1980, the Right Livelihood Award honors and supports those offering practical and exemplary answers to the most urgent challenges facing us today. It is presented annually in Stockholm, Sweden.

· The Kalidas Samman is an annual award given by the Madhya Pradesh government to recognize outstanding achievements in the arts.

· It is named after the renowned Sanskrit poet Kalidasa.

· The Kalidas Samman was first awarded in 1980.

· It was initially conferred in alternate years in four fields: Classical Music, Classical Dance, Theatre and Plastic Arts.

· From 1986-87 to 2008-09, the awards were presented in all four fields in most years, thereafter reverting to one person per year.

The Saraswati Samman is awarded for outstanding contribution to Indian literature.

The Saraswati Samman is an annual award for outstanding prose or poetry literary works in any Indian language listed in Schedule VIII of the Constitution of India.

It was established in 1991 by the K. K. Birla Foundation.

It consists of Rs.15 lakh, a citation and a plaque.
